correctness.rationale: The iid thinned-minimum coupling reproduces the exact transition kernel. Conditional strict lower-record indicators have the stated rank distribution. Strict stochastic ordering after a jump and an increasing future jump hazard prove all pairwise negative covariances. The published univariate PGF is explicitly transformed into Meixner polynomials and an independent generating-kernel proof establishes orthogonality and negative roots. For three times, exact symbolic differentiation yields three Rayleigh differences, each a positive prefactor times a square plus (8-8p-p^2)/4, so the stated sharp region and exceptional p=1 endpoint follow by the standard multiaffine real-stability criterion. 120 finite checks reproduce identities but are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The exact threshold classifies when a natural dependent Markov jump process enjoys the strongest standard multivariate negative-dependence property, while ordinary pairwise covariance and all finite count distributions remain well behaved. Three steps are provably minimal for the discrepancy, and the isolated restoration at p=1 exposes an interpretable atom/removal mechanism. This is a structural finite-horizon classification, not a routine change of parameters or arbitrary numerical example; higher-dimensional behavior is explicitly not claimed.
